ACM brings together computing educators, researchers, and professionals to inspire dialogue, share resources, and address the field's challenges. As the world’s largest computing society, ACM strengthens the profession's collective voice through strong leadership, promotion of the highest standards, and recognition of technical excellence. ACM supports the professional growth of its members by providing opportunities for life‐long learning, career development, and professional networking.

Founded at the dawn of the computer age, ACM’s reach extends to every part of the globe, with more than half of its nearly 100,000 members residing outside the U.S. Its growing membership has led to Councils in Europe, India, and China, fostering networking opportunities that strengthen ties within and across countries and technical communities. Their actions enhance ACM’s ability to raise awareness of computing’s important technical, educational, and social issues around the world.

Student Chapters provide unique opportunities for networking, mentoring and bonding over common interests. They provide support both within the student community and to local communities outside the institution.
Started in May 2015, NMAMIT ACM is actively conducts various technical and professional events like workshops, trainings, coding competitions, paper presentations, symposium, industry visits etc.

The Institution of Engineers (India), a national organization of engineers in India has more than a million members in 15 engineering disciplines in 114 centers or chapters in India and overseas; it is the world's largest multi-disciplinary engineering professional society in engineering and technology world. Established in 1920 in Kolkata it is acclaimed to have pioneered non-formal education in engineering. The Institution of Engineers (India) conducts an examination of its associate membership which is considered to be one part with B.E. / B.Tech. When contemplated as an eligibility qualification to write competitive examinations like the Indian Civil Service, Indian Engineering Services, GATE, etc., and for employment in Government, public and private sectors in India. This qualification is recognized by the Ministry of HRD, government of India, as equivalent to B.E./B.Tech. The Institution of Engineers (India) was incorporated by Royal Charter in 1935. It is currently headquartered in 8 Gokhale Road, Kolkata. NMAMIT has Institution of Engineers (India) students’ chapter for all the branches with About 1500 student members. This chapter has been conducting branch level, Institution level and intercollegiate level technical programs.

The Association of Computer Engineers (ACE), a club in NMAMIT Nitte, has been formed by the students of Computer Science and Engineering with an objective ofcreating a platform for students to participate in co-curricular activities and mingle with other students. The motive of this association is to bring out the hidden talent and to involve each member in various activities so that the youth exuberance should not be confined to the class room. Since its inception, the association is engaged in many events. The main such events are mentioned below:
Alumni Talk by Mr. Ranganatha Marathe, Principal Engineer at Cisco Systems and alumnus of the 1989-93 batch
As part of the Alumni Mentorship Series 2023, an engaging alumni talk was delivered by Mr. Ranganatha Marathe, Principal Engineer at Cisco Systems and alumnus of the 1989–93 batch.

In his session, Mr. Marathe highlighted the impact of networking technology in emerging markets, the advantages of cloud-native architectures, and emphasized the importance of continuous learning and professional networking in career growth.
The talk offered valuable industry insights, inspiring the student community while also strengthening the bond between alumni and the institution.
Alumni Talk by Mr. Vadiraja Bhatt, a distinguished alumnus of the institution and currently a Principal Engineer at Cloudera Inc

A highly informative and inspiring guest lecture was delivered by Mr. Vadiraja Bhatt, a distinguished alumnus of the institution and currently a Principal Engineer at Cloudera Inc. on September 5, 2024 at Sowparnika Hall, NMAMIT. With over three decades of experience in the tech industry, Mr. Bhatt brought a wealth of knowledge and insight to the session. The topic of the lecture, “Vector Databases,” explored a cutting-edge area of technology that is revolutionizing the way machines understand and process data, particularly in the fields of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning. He then delved into the fundamentals of vector databases, explaining how they differ from traditional databases by enabling semantic searches based on meaning rather than exact matches.

Mr. Bhatt also discussed the architectural components, high-dimensional data challenges, and performance requirements of these systems. Real-world applications such as intelligent chatbots, personalized recommendations, semantic search engines, and facial recognition systems were showcased to demonstrate the immense potential and current usage of vector databases in smart technologies.

The session concluded with an engaging Q&A where students inquired about career paths in AI, required skills, and practical ways to get started in the field. It provided a meaningful glimpse into the future of technology and empowered students to actively pursue knowledge and innovation in this evolving domain.
Talk on “Indian Space Programme”

Dr. A.G. Ananth, a former ISRO scientist, delivered a talk on the "Indian Space Programme" for 5th semester CSE students in the B and C sections on 31 October, 2023. The event covered satellite technology and the future of India's space industry, highlighting ISRO's contributions. The formative and engaging session included a Q&A, offering students valuable insights into space technology. The event inspired students with insights into the achievements and future of the Indian Space Programme.

A hands-on workshop on ReactJS was organized by CSE students Swasthik Shetty of 5th semester and Numan Naeem of 7th semester on 20 October 2022. The organizers shared their experience on react JS with the participants. Various aspects of react and their fundamentals such as their use in building web applications were discussed in the workshop.

The Association of Computer Engineers, in collaboration with ABHYUDAY – the Department of Counselling, Welfare, Training & Placement – conducted a placement talk on 8th December 2022 at Sambhram Hall for 5th semester CSE students. The interactive session featured placed students Anuroop Ravindra, R. P. Shamita, Prathamesh, and Rashmi Murali, who shared their placement journeys, resume-building tips, interview preparation strategies, and insights into various career opportunities.

The Association of Computer Engineers and ABHYUDAY – the Department of Counselling, Welfare, Training & Placement organised a placement talk for 5th semester CSE students at Sambhram Hall on on November 15, 2023.

The event featured an interactive session with placed students, who shared their placement journeys and valuable advice. Resource persons included Ardra Madhu (Samsung Semiconductors), Aaron Jevil Nazareth (Louisia AI), Gaurav Pai (Juniper Networks), Swasthik Shetty (Redbus), Vasudha G (HPE), and Chinmaya Shyamaraj (Nutanix), all final-year CSE students. They provided insights on resume building, placement preparation, and interview strategies, helping students better understand job market challenges and effectively navigate the placement process.

CODE RELAY, a technical event conducted to provide a platform for students to showcase their coding skills on 10th December 2022. The event was open to all branches. The event saw teams compete in two rounds: (1) Aptitude – a team-based challenge, and (2) Coding – a relay-style contest. Winners were declared based on the highest team scores, and exciting cash prizes were awarded.
Social Outreach Programs
Visit to Vijetha Vasathiyuta Visshesa Saale

ACE organized an outreach program at Vijetha Vasathiyuta Visshesa Shale, a special school for over 100 students of varying ages on May 2nd, 2024. Around 30 students attended the program. Dr. Kanthi Harish, principal of the school warmly welcomed the ACE team. The event began with a brief address from Dr. Harish, followed by Dr. Pradeep Kanchan, Head of ACE, who emphasized empathy and connection.

ACE students engaged with special school children through interactive activities such as dancing and a passing-the-ball game, fostering joy, inclusivity, teamwork, and coordination. Winners were rewarded with chocolates and stationery items. The event, filled with laughter and friendship, reflected generosity and kindness, leaving a lasting impact on the school community.
The IoT and Web Development Workshop, held on November 11, 2024, at Sundar Puranik Memorial Government High School

The IoT and Web Development Workshop was held at Sundar Puranik Memorial Government High School on 11 November 2024. The outreach program was aimed at introducing school students to emerging technologies. The session featured engaging demonstrations on IoT components and sensors, allowing students to visualize how these tools connect the physical and digital worlds.

A beginner-friendly introduction to web development familiarized participants with the basics of website creation. Students actively participated in discussions and hands-on activities, showcasing great curiosity and enthusiasm. The workshop not only educated but also inspired young minds to explore the fields of technology and innovation, leaving a lasting impact and igniting a spark for future learning.
Visit to Parpale Ashram

The ACE Association organized a visit to Parpale Ashram (Senior Citizens’ Home) on 21st November 2024 as part of its community outreach initiative. The objective of the program was to bring joy, companionship, and a sense of togetherness to the residents of the home. The event commenced with interactive activities designed to foster engagement between the students and the senior citizens. Games and simple physical exercises were conducted, creating an atmosphere of fun and relaxation. A particularly memorable part of the program was the sharing of life experiences by the residents, whose stories, filled with wisdom and emotion, provided students with valuable lessons in resilience, gratitude, and the importance of human connections.

The program further evolved into a celebration of unity with music and dance, where both students and residents participated enthusiastically, spreading cheer and positivity. The visit concluded with the distribution of refreshments and wholesome food, marking the end of a day filled with warmth, care, and mutual appreciation.

The Finite Loop Club (FLC) is the official institute-level coding community of NMAM Institute of Technology, Nitte. Founded in 2016 by Dr. Shashank Shetty, Dr.Puneeth R. P., and Mr. Krishna Prasad Rao, the club has evolved from a hobby initiative into a vibrant platform for aspiring developers and tech enthusiasts across all departments. It fosters creativity, collaboration, and innovation through hands-on workshops, real-time consultancy projects, and an active Discord community that promotes peer-to-peer learning. Over the years, FLC has become an integral part of NMAMIT’s tech culture, inspiring students and equipping them with the skills to become future-ready software professionals.

content_blocks.text: The Department of Computer Science & Engineering, established in 1986, offers UG, PG and research (leading to M.Sc. and Ph.D.) programs. The Department practices outcome-based education since 2014. With state-of-the-art laboratories and other supporting facilities to provide enhanced learning environment, the Department boasts of well qualified teaching faculty with rich research, teaching and industrial experience.

The Department has excellent placement track record in reputed industries with an average of 80 – 85% placement of eligible students over the years. The Department regularly conducts audit courses, and special courses on advanced topics, to bridge the gap between the curriculum and the need of the industry. The Department offers M.Tech programs in Computer Science & Engineering and Cyber Security. From the year 2022-23 M.Tech program is under Nitte University.

ACM brings together computing educators, researchers, and professionals to inspire dialogue, share resources, and address the field's challenges. As the world’s largest computing society, ACM strengthens the profession's collective voice through strong leadership, promotion of the highest standards, and recognition of technical excellence. ACM supports the professional growth of its members by providing opportunities for life‐long learning, career development, and professional networking.

Founded at the dawn of the computer age, ACM’s reach extends to every part of the globe, with more than half of its nearly 100,000 members residing outside the U.S. Its growing membership has led to Councils in Europe, India, and China, fostering networking opportunities that strengthen ties within and across countries and technical communities. Their actions enhance ACM’s ability to raise awareness of computing’s important technical, educational, and social issues around the world.

Student Chapters provide unique opportunities for networking, mentoring and bonding over common interests. They provide support both within the student community and to local communities outside the institution.
Started in May 2015, NMAMIT ACM is actively conducts various technical and professional events like workshops, trainings, coding competitions, paper presentations, symposium, industry visits etc.

The Institution of Engineers (India), a national organization of engineers in India has more than a million members in 15 engineering disciplines in 114 centers or chapters in India and overseas; it is the world's largest multi-disciplinary engineering professional society in engineering and technology world. Established in 1920 in Kolkata it is acclaimed to have pioneered non-formal education in engineering. The Institution of Engineers (India) conducts an examination of its associate membership which is considered to be one part with B.E. / B.Tech. When contemplated as an eligibility qualification to write competitive examinations like the Indian Civil Service, Indian Engineering Services, GATE, etc., and for employment in Government, public and private sectors in India. This qualification is recognized by the Ministry of HRD, government of India, as equivalent to B.E./B.Tech. The Institution of Engineers (India) was incorporated by Royal Charter in 1935. It is currently headquartered in 8 Gokhale Road, Kolkata. NMAMIT has Institution of Engineers (India) students’ chapter for all the branches with About 1500 student members. This chapter has been conducting branch level, Institution level and intercollegiate level technical programs.

As part of the Alumni Mentorship Series 2023, an engaging alumni talk was delivered by Mr. Ranganatha Marathe, Principal Engineer at Cisco Systems and alumnus of the 1989–93 batch.

In his session, Mr. Marathe highlighted the impact of networking technology in emerging markets, the advantages of cloud-native architectures, and emphasized the importance of continuous learning and professional networking in career growth.
The talk offered valuable industry insights, inspiring the student community while also strengthening the bond between alumni and the institution.
Alumni Talk by Mr. Vadiraja Bhatt, a distinguished alumnus of the institution and currently a Principal Engineer at Cloudera Inc

A highly informative and inspiring guest lecture was delivered by Mr. Vadiraja Bhatt, a distinguished alumnus of the institution and currently a Principal Engineer at Cloudera Inc. on September 5, 2024 at Sowparnika Hall, NMAMIT. With over three decades of experience in the tech industry, Mr. Bhatt brought a wealth of knowledge and insight to the session. The topic of the lecture, “Vector Databases,” explored a cutting-edge area of technology that is revolutionizing the way machines understand and process data, particularly in the fields of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning. He then delved into the fundamentals of vector databases, explaining how they differ from traditional databases by enabling semantic searches based on meaning rather than exact matches.

Mr. Bhatt also discussed the architectural components, high-dimensional data challenges, and performance requirements of these systems. Real-world applications such as intelligent chatbots, personalized recommendations, semantic search engines, and facial recognition systems were showcased to demonstrate the immense potential and current usage of vector databases in smart technologies.

The session concluded with an engaging Q&A where students inquired about career paths in AI, required skills, and practical ways to get started in the field. It provided a meaningful glimpse into the future of technology and empowered students to actively pursue knowledge and innovation in this evolving domain.

The ACE Association organized a visit to Parpale Ashram (Senior Citizens’ Home) on 21st November 2024 as part of its community outreach initiative. Games and simple physical exercises were conducted, creating an atmosphere of fun and relaxation. The program further evolved into a celebration of unity with music and dance, where both students and residents participated enthusiastically, spreading cheer and positivity. The visit concluded with the distribution of refreshments and wholesome food, marking the end of a day filled with warmth, care, and mutual appreciation.

content_blocks.text: At NMAM Institute of Technology (NMAMIT), Nitte, the Department of Physical Education plays a vital role in fostering holistic growth of students. Along with academic excellence, the department emphasizes fitness, discipline, and teamwork, encouraging students to actively participate in sports and recreational activities.

Our state-of-the-art B.C. Alva Sports Complex serves as a hub for sporting excellence, offering world-class infrastructure that enables students to pursue both indoor and outdoor games with enthusiasm and passion.

items: International Standard Basketball Court with wooden flooring.

Cricket Field with 3 centre pitches and 3 practice pitches.
Multiple Courts: Volleyball, Handball, Basketball, and Throwball.

content_blocks.text: At NMAMIT, we believe in rewarding talent and motivating our athletes to reach greater heights. To support and encourage student participation in sports at intercollegiate, university, national, and international levels, the institution provides a wide range of incentives.

items: Free Boarding & Lodging for participants in intercollegiate, inter-university, and open competitions.
Coaching Camp Support with free boarding and lodging for day scholars during training sessions.
Sports Kits including T-shirts and shorts.
Track Suits for inter-university participants.
Cash Awards for outstanding achievers.
Medical & Physiotherapy Support free of cost.
Expert Coaching by inviting external coaches and event specialists.

title: Department of Computer Science (Cyber Security) - NITTE

headings.text: B.Tech in Computer Science & Engineering (Cyber Security)
For any information regarding the admissions, mail us at: info@nitte.edu.in

paragraphs: The Bachelor of Technology in Computer Science and Engineering (Cyber Security) programme, introduced in the academic year 2023–24 under Nitte Deemed to be University, is designed to nurture proficient professionals in the rapidly evolving field of Cyber Security. With the digital landscape expanding at an unprecedented pace, cybersecurity has emerged as a mission-critical discipline for organisations across sectors. According to the Data Security Council of India (DSCI), the nation currently faces a demand-supply gap of nearly one million cybersecurity professionals, highlighting the urgent need for skilled experts in this domain.

This B.Tech program at NMAM Institute of Technology integrates core and advanced concepts of Computer Science and Engineering with specialised courses in Cyber Security, ensuring a well-rounded technical foundation. The curriculum equips students with the competencies required to excel both as software engineers and as cybersecurity specialists, enabling them to pursue rewarding global career opportunities. Through the Cyber Security and Analysis certification, students gain an additional professional edge, preparing them to work with leading organisations worldwide.

The department emphasises research and innovation, providing avenues for students to engage in cutting-edge projects, collaborate with the Centre of Excellence, and receive hands-on training from industry experts. These experiences foster both technical proficiency and professional confidence.

To be a premier Department of Computer Science and Engineering in the field of Cyber Security, committed to providing high-quality education, impactful research, and strong employability skills, thereby developing ethical, competent, and socially responsible professionals and entrepreneurs who contribute to community development.

Department of Cybersecurity on 27 October 2025

The Department of Cyber Security, NMAM Institute of Technology, in association with PROTON and the Rotary Club Nitte (Zone-5, District 3182), organised a week-long Cyber Security Awareness Program (CSAP) from 27th to 31st October 2025 under the initiative “CyberCare: Awareness for the Next Generation”. The CyberCare Program was designed to educate school and college students on cyber hygiene, online safety, and responsible digital behaviour. The awareness sessions were organised across five institutions — Dr. NSAM Kannada Medium School, Nitte; Government High School, Kalya; Government High School, Belman; Government PU College, Belman; and Government Primary School, Kallambadi Padav.

Each session commenced with an inaugural ceremony, featuring addresses by eminent dignitaries including Dr. Roshan Fernandes, Rtn. Dr. Raghunandan K. R., and faculty coordinators Ms. Ashmi Kotian, Mr. S. Shyam Kumar, and Ms. Varshitha. Following the inauguration, student presenters from PROTON delivered highly engaging and informative sessions covering topics such as cybersecurity fundamentals, phishing awareness, social media scams, cyberbullying, and safe online practices. The sessions were further enriched through interactive quizzes and activity-based learning facilitated by PROTON members, which enhanced student participation and reinforced key learning outcomes. Guest speakers including Rtn. Vignesh Shenoy, Mr. Vincent Vinod, and Mr. Prasanna M. S., Sub-Inspector from Karkala Police Station, provided real-world perspectives on prevailing cyber threats and effective preventive strategies.The valedictory ceremony held at Government Primary School, Kallambadi Padav marked the successful culmination of the campaign, with dignitaries commending the initiative’s educational value, outreach, and tangible impact on young digital citizens.In conclusion, the CyberCare Program significantly contributed to raising awareness on digital safety and empowering students to navigate the online world with responsibility, vigilance, and informed decision-making.
By PROTON, Association of Department of Cybersecurity on 25 October 2025

The PROTON Association of the Cyber Security Department organised a creative and engaging event titled “Fish Tank (Reverse Shark Tank)” on 25th October 2025 at Shambhavi Hall, APJ Block. Conducted from 9:00 AM to 12:30 PM, the event witnessed enthusiastic participation from seven teams, each comprising two to three members. Designed to foster creativity, humour, communication, and teamwork, the event challenged participants to pitch imaginative and unconventional products as revolutionary inventions. In Round 1 – Product Pitch, teams presented their quirky concepts, demonstrating originality, persuasive ability, and presentation skills to captivate the judges. Round 2 – The Twist Challenge introduced unexpected scenarios, compelling participants to adapt swiftly and exhibit spontaneous problem-solving and presence of mind. The light-hearted yet intellectually stimulating atmosphere kept the audience and judges thoroughly engaged. Through its humorous and interactive approach, the event successfully promoted confidence building, creative marketing, and quick thinking among students. Concluding at 12:30 PM, “Fish Tank” left participants inspired, entertained, and enriched by the experience. Overall, the event served as a unique fusion of innovation, laughter, and learning, showcasing the department’s commitment to experiential and skill-based education.
By PROTON, Association of Department of Cybersecurity on 11 October 2025

The CTF event was coordinated by Mr. Rishi Bhati, President of PROTON, along with the core members. It aimed to provide students with real-world cybersecurity experience through hands-on problem-solving and teamwork. The competition was held across multiple labs of NMAMIT, Nitte ensuring a smooth and secure setup. Participants competed in challenges related to cryptography, web exploitation, forensics and reverse engineering. Around 100 students participated enthusiastically, showcasing analytical and technical skills. The event began at 9:45 AM and concluded at 12:45 PM after three hours of intense problem-solving. The prize distribution ceremony was held on 13th October 2025, where winners received cash prizes and certificates. The event was a great success, fostering technical learning, collaboration, and competitive spirit among participants..
Department of Cybersecurity on 07 October 2025

The Department of Cybersecurity conducted a workshop titled “From Idea to Publication: Writing an Effective Research Paper” at ADL04, SMV Block (AIDS Department), facilitated by Dr. Anisha P. Rodrigues and Mrs. Divya Jennifer Dsouza. The session focused on research methodology and LaTeX-based paper formatting, guiding participants through essential stages such as topic selection, literature review, citation practices, and document structuring.

The hands-on LaTeX session provided practical experience in formatting equations, images, and references, helping students gain technical proficiency in academic writing. Coordinated by Mr. Shyam Kumar and Ms. Ashmi K. Kotian, the workshop received excellent feedback for its clarity, practical approach, and contribution to strengthening students’ research and writing competencies.
Department of Cybersecurity on 27 March 2025

Cybersecurity students had the privilege of hosting Mr. Takashi Tsujiuchi, CEO of Findnext Co., Ltd., Japan, along with Prof. Harikrishna Bhat, Ms. Yasuko Sato, and Dr. Roshan Fernandes, Head of the Cybersecurity Department. The session offered valuable insights into Japan’s growing demand for cybersecurity professionals and highlighted global career opportunities in the field.

Mr. Tsujiuchi emphasised the need for international talent and the increasing significance of digital security, while Prof. Bhat guided students on the recruitment process and key skill sets required for placements in Japan. An engaging Q&A session helped clarify job expectations and cultural nuances of working in Japan.The event served as an inspiration for students to sharpen their technical competencies and pursue global opportunities in cybersecurity.
Proton – Department of Cybersecurity on 25 January 2025

PROTON, in association with the Computer Society of India (CSI), organised “Ctrl + Alt Code”, a coding and aptitude competition aimed at testing participants’ logical reasoning and programming expertise. The event comprised two rounds — Aptitude and Coding — and attracted 16 enthusiastic teams (41 participants) eager to demonstrate their skills.The first round evaluated reasoning and mathematical aptitude, while the second round challenged the top teams with six coding problems, enhanced by exciting power-ups that added a strategic edge. Squad 12 from the Department of Research and Development emerged as the winners, claiming a cash prize of INR 2000.Overall, the event was both engaging and intellectually stimulating, fostering teamwork, analytical thinking, and coding excellence among participants.
Dr. Roshan Fernandes, Professor & Head, Department of Cyber Security - 16 January 2025

Proton Association of the Department of Cyber Security, NMAMIT, organised a Research Paper Writing Workshop to equip students with essential research and academic writing skills. The session, led by Dr. Roshan Fernandes (Professor & Head, Cyber Security), covered the complete research process from identifying problem statements to defining future scope. Over 50 students from various semesters actively participated, gaining insights into literature surveys, methodology design, result analysis and effective paper structuring. The event successfully provided students with a clear framework and practical guidance for initiating and presenting their research effectively.

PROTON – The Association of Department of Cybersecurity

PROTON is the official student association of the Department of Cybersecurity at NMAM Institute of Technology, Nitte. It was established with the objective of fostering learning, collaboration, and innovation in the field of cybersecurity. The association serves as a vital link between academic learning and industry practices by providing students with practical exposure to cutting-edge tools, methodologies, and real-world security challenges.

Throughout the academic year, PROTON organises a range of impactful events such as technical workshops, Capture the Flag (CTF) competitions, expert talks, and cybersecurity awareness sessions. Its flagship event, Cyber Insight, offers participants hands-on experience in ethical hacking, digital forensics, and cyber defence strategies. Other signature initiatives include Cyberloop, Ctrl Alt + Code, and the Workshop on Research Papers, all designed to enhance technical competence and research aptitude among students.

In addition to its technical endeavours, PROTON actively engages in community outreach through Cybersecurity Awareness Programs (CSAP) conducted in nearby schools, aiming to educate young learners on safe online practices and responsible digital citizenship.

Guided by dedicated faculty advisors, the association is currently led by its dynamic Core Team (2025–26), headed by President Rishi Bhati. Looking ahead, PROTON envisions expanding its impact by hosting inter-collegiate cybersecurity challenges, collaborating with industry experts, and promoting research-driven projects, thereby empowering students to excel as competent cybersecurity professionals in the rapidly evolving digital landscape.

content_blocks.text: The Bachelor of Technology in Computer Science and Engineering (Cyber Security) programme, introduced in the academic year 2023–24 under Nitte Deemed to be University, is designed to nurture proficient professionals in the rapidly evolving field of Cyber Security. With the digital landscape expanding at an unprecedented pace, cybersecurity has emerged as a mission-critical discipline for organisations across sectors. According to the Data Security Council of India (DSCI), the nation currently faces a demand-supply gap of nearly one million cybersecurity professionals, highlighting the urgent need for skilled experts in this domain.

This B.Tech program at NMAM Institute of Technology integrates core and advanced concepts of Computer Science and Engineering with specialised courses in Cyber Security, ensuring a well-rounded technical foundation. The curriculum equips students with the competencies required to excel both as software engineers and as cybersecurity specialists, enabling them to pursue rewarding global career opportunities. Through the Cyber Security and Analysis certification, students gain an additional professional edge, preparing them to work with leading organisations worldwide.

The department emphasises research and innovation, providing avenues for students to engage in cutting-edge projects, collaborate with the Centre of Excellence, and receive hands-on training from industry experts. These experiences foster both technical proficiency and professional confidence.

To be a premier Department of Computer Science and Engineering in the field of Cyber Security, committed to providing high-quality education, impactful research, and strong employability skills, thereby developing ethical, competent, and socially responsible professionals and entrepreneurs who contribute to community development.

content_blocks.text: The Department of Cyber Security, NMAM Institute of Technology, in association with PROTON and the Rotary Club Nitte (Zone-5, District 3182), organised a week-long Cyber Security Awareness Program (CSAP) from 27th to 31st October 2025 under the initiative “CyberCare: Awareness for the Next Generation”. The CyberCare Program was designed to educate school and college students on cyber hygiene, online safety, and responsible digital behaviour. The awareness sessions were organised across five institutions — Dr. NSAM Kannada Medium School, Nitte; Government High School, Kalya; Government High School, Belman; Government PU College, Belman; and Government Primary School, Kallambadi Padav.

Each session commenced with an inaugural ceremony, featuring addresses by eminent dignitaries including Dr. Roshan Fernandes, Rtn. Dr. Raghunandan K. R., and faculty coordinators Ms. Ashmi Kotian, Mr. S. Shyam Kumar, and Ms. Varshitha. Following the inauguration, student presenters from PROTON delivered highly engaging and informative sessions covering topics such as cybersecurity fundamentals, phishing awareness, social media scams, cyberbullying, and safe online practices. The sessions were further enriched through interactive quizzes and activity-based learning facilitated by PROTON members, which enhanced student participation and reinforced key learning outcomes. Guest speakers including Rtn. Vignesh Shenoy, Mr. Vincent Vinod, and Mr. Prasanna M. S., Sub-Inspector from Karkala Police Station, provided real-world perspectives on prevailing cyber threats and effective preventive strategies.The valedictory ceremony held at Government Primary School, Kallambadi Padav marked the successful culmination of the campaign, with dignitaries commending the initiative’s educational value, outreach, and tangible impact on young digital citizens.In conclusion, the CyberCare Program significantly contributed to raising awareness on digital safety and empowering students to navigate the online world with responsibility, vigilance, and informed decision-making.

Participants competed in challenges related to cryptography, web exploitation, forensics and reverse engineering. The prize distribution ceremony was held on 13th October 2025, where winners received cash prizes and certificates. The event was a great success, fostering technical learning, collaboration, and competitive spirit among participants..

Rodrigues and Mrs. Divya Jennifer Dsouza. The session focused on research methodology and LaTeX-based paper formatting, guiding participants through essential stages such as topic selection, literature review, citation practices, and document structuring.

The hands-on LaTeX session provided practical experience in formatting equations, images, and references, helping students gain technical proficiency in academic writing. Coordinated by Mr. Shyam Kumar and Ms. Ashmi K. Kotian, the workshop received excellent feedback for its clarity, practical approach, and contribution to strengthening students’ research and writing competencies.

Cybersecurity students had the privilege of hosting Mr. Takashi Tsujiuchi, CEO of Findnext Co., Ltd., Japan, along with Prof. Harikrishna Bhat, Ms. Yasuko Sato, and Dr. Roshan Fernandes, Head of the Cybersecurity Department. The session offered valuable insights into Japan’s growing demand for cybersecurity professionals and highlighted global career opportunities in the field.

Mr. Tsujiuchi emphasised the need for international talent and the increasing significance of digital security, while Prof. Bhat guided students on the recruitment process and key skill sets required for placements in Japan. An engaging Q&A session helped clarify job expectations and cultural nuances of working in Japan.The event served as an inspiration for students to sharpen their technical competencies and pursue global opportunities in cybersecurity.

The team showcased exceptional innovation and technical skills, securing Second Place in the competition. They were also awarded a cash prize of ₹6,000.

Shravya R and Sujnan D Devadiga from the Department of Cyber Security, along with Neelima Bhaktha from the Department of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, secured Second Place in the Flinders University AI Competition 2026, held at Ocean Pearl, Mangalore. The competition featured a hackathon focused on designing and developing impactful AI-based prototypes. The team demonstrated strong technical expertise and innovation, earning them this notable achievement.

Niharika(Cybersecurity), Harshitha P Sanil and Gowrika Alva (Information Science) and Sahana Acharya (CSE) from team Debug Divas won the Open Innovation Track at Hackfest 2026, organised by the Finite Loop Club, NMAMIT. The team was awarded a cash prize of Rs. 10000.

Bhaveesh N Shetty from the Department of Cyber Security was awarded as the Best Outstanding Sports Person during the Annual Sports and Games Competitions 2025–2026 at N.M.A.M. Institute of Technology, Nitte.

Mr. Sujnan D. Devadiga and Mr. Aditya Bhat K., students of the VI Semester, Department of Cyber Security, secured the Runner-Up position at the Mangaluru Regional Finals of the 17th Edition of TCS TechBytes. The event was organised by Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) in association with the Board for IT Education Standards (BITES) and hosted at Sahyadri College of Engineering and Management, Mangaluru.

The students demonstrated exceptional technical competence, problem-solving abilities, and teamwork throughout the competition. Their remarkable achievement brought laurels to the institution and was further recognised through coverage in The Times of India, highlighting their success and the institution's commitment to academic and professional excellence.

The Department of Cyber Security proudly congratulates Dr. Manjunath Kamath K, Associate Professor, on being honored with the Prestigious Best Ph.D. Thesis Award by the Board of IT Education Standards, an autonomous body under the Government of Karnataka, in association with IISc Bengaluru and leading academic and IT industry partners. His award-winning Ph.D. thesis titled “A Framework for Reversible Data Hiding in Video Steganography” was completed under Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU), Belagavi, under the esteemed guidance of Dr. R. Sanjeev Kunte (J.N.N. College of Engineering, Shivamogga). The research focuses on enhancing secure information embedding in videos while maintaining visual quality, contributing significantly to modern digital security and privacy. The award was presented on 24 January 2026 at the Bosch Learning Center, Bengaluru. This achievement brings great pride to the department and highlights the institution’s commitment to excellence in research and innovation.

Aditya Bhat and Sujnan Devadiga of III-year Cybersecurity secured first place in the Technical Quiz conducted as part of the 21st Karnataka State Level ISTE Student Convention 2025 at Yenepoya Institute of Technology, Mangalore.

The Department of Cyber Security with Proton Association and NSS IT Wing, NMAM Institute of Technology, Nitte (Deemed to be University) has secured the second prize in the Awareness Video Competition conducted by Udupi District Police as part of Cyber Awareness Month – October 2025, for spreading awareness on Cyber Safety and Online Responsibility. The prize certificate was handed over during the program held on 31 October 2025 at Udupi District Police Department, Udupi. Dr Roshan Fernandes, Ms. Ashmi Kotian from the department of Cyber Security along with students Mr. Rishi Bhati, Mr. Mohd Shaadaan, Mr. Om, Mr. Keerthan, Mr. Gaurav received the honor from Shri. Hariram Shankar, IPS, Superintendent of Police, Udupi District. Mr. Bhavin, Ms. Spoorthy, Ms. Anusha, Ms. Sindhura, Ms. Pratheeksha, Ms. Prachi have contributed for this reel.

II-year B.Tech CSE (Cyber Security) students Ms. Erum Hanif and Mr. Calvin Dsouza secured the First Runner-Up position at the “Acethon Hackathon” hosted by the ACE Association, Department of CSE, NMAMIT (Deemed to be University), Nitte, on 11 October 2025. Their achievement reflects strong technical competence, creativity, and commitment to excellence in the field of cyber security.

An interdisciplinary team comprising Vruddith R. Shetty, Pratheeksha (III Year B.Tech CSE – Cyber Security), Gaurav B. Shet (CSE), and Niyuktha Sandeep (Biotechnology) secured First Place in the Cybersecurity track at Srinathon 2.0, an international 24-hour hackathon hosted by Srinivas Institute of Technology on 9 October 2025.

An II-year B.Tech CSE (Cyber Security) team comprising Adarsh H. N., Ravi Shashi Netre, Vamshaj Rai, and Jeevan Nayak secured Second Place in the Cybersecurity track at Srinathon 2.0, an international-level 24-hour hackathon hosted by Srinivas Institute of Technology on 9 October 2025.

A team comprising Aditya Bhat K and Sujnan D. Devadiga secured First Place in the Luminiq Quiz Competition conducted as part of Udbhava 2025 at the Nitte Institute of Professional Education, Mangalore, on 8 October 2025.

The Department of Cyber Security reported notable achievements at the Cyber Security Bootcamp conducted by NITK Surathkal in collaboration with CySeck (IISc). Mubashar (V Semester), Ravi (III Semester), Bhavin (V Semester), and Amithesh (V Semester) secured top performer positions, ranking 6th, 8th, 9th, and 10th respectively, in the CTF competition held among 300+ participants.
PROTON – The Association of Department of Cybersecurity

PROTON is the official student association of the Department of Cybersecurity at NMAM Institute of Technology, Nitte. It was established with the objective of fostering learning, collaboration, and innovation in the field of cybersecurity. The association serves as a vital link between academic learning and industry practices by providing students with practical exposure to cutting-edge tools, methodologies, and real-world security challenges.

Throughout the academic year, PROTON organises a range of impactful events such as technical workshops, Capture the Flag (CTF) competitions, expert talks, and cybersecurity awareness sessions. Its flagship event, Cyber Insight, offers participants hands-on experience in ethical hacking, digital forensics, and cyber defence strategies. Other signature initiatives include Cyberloop, Ctrl Alt + Code, and the Workshop on Research Papers, all designed to enhance technical competence and research aptitude among students.

In addition to its technical endeavours, PROTON actively engages in community outreach through Cybersecurity Awareness Programs (CSAP) conducted in nearby schools, aiming to educate young learners on safe online practices and responsible digital citizenship.

Guided by dedicated faculty advisors, the association is currently led by its dynamic Core Team (2025–26), headed by President Rishi Bhati. Looking ahead, PROTON envisions expanding its impact by hosting inter-collegiate cybersecurity challenges, collaborating with industry experts, and promoting research-driven projects, thereby empowering students to excel as competent cybersecurity professionals in the rapidly evolving digital landscape.

The Department of Cybersecurity, NMAM Institute of Technology (NMAMIT), inaugurated its Centre of Excellence in collaboration with Vill Design, Japan, on 15 September 2025. The event was graced by Dr. M. S. Moodithaya, Vice Chancellor, Nitte (Deemed to be University), as Chief Guest, along with delegates from Vill Design Japan Mr. Naotaka Taguchi, Mr. Hiroshi Nakayama and Mr. Takashi Tsujiuchi. Prof. Harikrishna Bhat highlighted NMAMIT’s collaborations with Japan.

The guests appreciated the Department’s vision and expressed confidence that the Vill Design Lab would foster innovation and excellence in Cybersecurity. The Centre offers services including Web and Network Penetration Testing, EDR and Microsoft 365 Testing and Web and Mobile Application Development.

The Centre operates under the guidance of Dr. Roshan Fernandes, supported by Ms. Shivani Pai and Mr. Hemraj Narwariya as full-time staff members. Student interns from B.Tech (Cybersecurity)—Mr. Rishi Bhati, Mr. Bhavin Adyanthaya, Mr. Sandeep Pai, Ms. Niharika, Ms. Gauthami M, Mr. Shaamak Madhwaraj Bolar, Ms. Shravya R, and Mr. Yashraj—are actively engaged in this initiative.

paragraphs: The Civil Engineering Department started in 1987 with a UG Programme with an intake of 60. Since the Academic year 2012-13, the intake has been increased to 120. The intake for the current Academic Year (2024-25) is 60. Two year Post Graduation programme M.Tech in Construction Technology was started in 2010 with an intake of 18 and M.Tech in Structural Engineering in the year 2017 with an intake of 24. The Department is also recognized as a Research Centre offering M.Sc. (Engg.) and Ph.D. programmes with 9 research scholars pursuing their Ph. D. In addition, the Department Students' Association (OCEAN) organizes seminars, workshops, educational tours and design competitions for Civil Engineering students. It also conducts Leadership Training, Personality Development Training and Entrepreneurship Development Programmes. The Department has taken up Karnataka State Council for Science & Technology (KSCST) funded projects and is also working on developing Masonry blocks and Paver blocks using Industrial waste materials under Karnataka New Age Incubation Centre, NMAMIT funded by the Department of IT, BT and S & T, government of Karnataka.

The department of Civil Engineering, NMAM Institute of Technology, Nitte an off-campus centre of Nitte Deemed to be University, signed an MOU with L&T EduTech under College Connect scheme to provide practical and application-oriented learning to make learners job-ready. As more and more recruiters look for job-ready candidates, the program provides live industry exposure through simulated laboratories and immersive programs. The program aims to provide physical immersion programs, thereby enriching the learning process. This MoU empowers faculty and facilitates industry-academia collaboration in undertaking industry-led research programs.

Larsen & Toubro is an Indian multinational engaged in Engineering Procurement and Construction Projects, Hi-Tech Manufacturing and Services. It operates in over 50 countries worldwide. L&T Construction, India's largest construction organisation and ranked among the world's top contractors, has been over the past seven decades transforming cityscapes and landscapes with structures of immense size and grandeur. The L&T EduTech MoU enables the NMAMIT Civil Engineering Graduates form the academic year 2023 securing B. Tech. degree combined with a specialization in Transportation Infrastructure Engineering certificate from L& T EduTech. It is a career integrated program first of its kind in the state of Karnataka.

In the world of engineering and technology, change and advancements are happening at the speed of light. Academia needs to keep pace with this change and career professionals need to adapt. The vision for L&T EduTech is to be a bridge between academia and industry, between career professionals and ever-changing technology. L&T EduTech firmly believes that, only when these need gaps are filled, we will have truly empowered and knowledgeable workforce that will lead India in the future.
To uphold the Department as a leader in community development through innovation and excellence in diverse areas of Civil Engineering to meet the global challenges and market demands

PO1: Engineering knowledge: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.

PO2: Problem analysis: Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.

PO3: Design/development of solutions: Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.

P04: Conduct investigations of complex problems: Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions.

PO5: Modern tool usage: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools including prediction and modeling to complex engineering activities with an understanding of the limitations.

PO6: The engineer and society: Apply reasoning informed by the contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional engineering practice.

PO7: Environment and sustainability: Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable development.
PO8: Ethics: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice.
P09: Individual and team work: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings.

PO10:Communication: Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large, such as, being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and receive clear instructions.

PO11: Project management and finance: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering and management principles and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.
PO12: Life-long learning: Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.

content_blocks.text: ORGANIZATION OF CIVIL ENGINEERING ASPIRANTS OF NITTE (OCEAN)

The aim of the Organization of Civil Engineering Aspirants of Nitte (OCEAN) is to promote educational, social, cultural and sporting activities amongst Civil Engineering students. In addition, it also provides opportunities to build professional leadership qualities, team work, and personality development and exhibit technical skills. Through consistent student activities, they learn more about civil engineering aspects to meet community expectations. Students are also encouraged to participate in techno cultural events held at various levels. It inspires students to represent the department at recruitment, industry and alumni events across the society.

title: MTech in CSE - NMAMIT
paragraphs: M.Tech program in Computer Science & Engineering was started in the academic year 2003-04. Total student intake for the program is 25. Some of the subjects that will be studied during the first two semesters are Machine Learning, Multi core Architecture and Parallel Programming, Design Thinking,Advanced Databases, Cloud Computing, Big Data and Data analytics. Few subjects are totally designed and handled by Industry experts. Electives are designed under different groups and are targeted tocater for the emerging trends in Computer Science and aligned with the industry needs. The students,during their 2nd year will get an opportunity to carry out their internship in industries with which an academic association has been established. Thus there will be enhanced placement opportunities in niche areas. Research focused inputs are also provided during the program so that students can even get into further research specific studies. Students are also having an option to carry out their research based project under the supervision of an experienced faculty. There are provisions to enhance the technical skills by taking the Audit courses and interdisciplinary skills by opting for Open elective courses.
Pursuing Excellence, Empowering people, Partnering in CommunityDevelopment

During 2022-23 students have been placed the companies like Dell, Ingersoll Rand, Continental Automotive Components, Textron India Private limited, Robert Bosch BGSW

M.Tech graduates can find opportunities as Scientist, Consultant, Professor, Research Expert, Technical Analyst, Software Engineer. They can serve in Engineering, Academic Institutions, Research Institutions, Sales and Marketing Firms, IT/Software Companies.

title: MTech in CCT - NMAMIT
paragraphs: The M.Tech in Construction Technology program was started in the year 2010, with an intake of 18 students. This inter-disciplinary programme is designed to suit the needs of students from India and other countries in the Afro-Asian region for undertaking professional responsibilities, demanding high proficiency in skills of application of latest technology, human resource management, project finance, business management, contracts management, project evaluation and appraisal, asset management, infrastructure management, financing, design, construction and operation and maintenance, with an objective to improve the economic, environmental and social sustainability of the infrastructure systems along with soft skills like MS Project, Primavera, BIMs etc. This programme provide opportunity to combine theory with practical experience and research work. The electives offered in the Programme allow engineers from different disciplines to select specialised project management subjects to enhance their subject knowledge in tune with careers of their choice. The curriculum has been reviewed from time to time to incorporate the latest advancements in Construction, Real Estate, Infrastructure, management skills and soft skills to build a strong competence in the diversified area. This programme also very much helpful for the graduates who wants to run family owned companies or to start their own business, companies or consultancy.

This programme provides opportunities for students to carryout internship, projects, research and skill development etc., anywhere in the globe of their choice. Experts and industries from both national and international levels like Geosmart International Pte.Ltd, Singapore, M/s Srishti Ventures and M/s Accretgeo etc., will provide teaching, training and placement assistance.
To uphold the Department as a leader in community development through innovation and excellence in diverse areas of Civil Engineering to meet the global challenges and market demands

The department is actively involved in consultancy of Civil Engineering structures. The major areas are structural design, determination of SBC, Mix design, third party inspection of different Civil Engineering structures etc. Students are actively participating in the design and analysis of structures.

title: Non-Technical Clubs - NMAMIT
paragraphs: Omkara Bhajana Club is dedicated to preserving and promoting the spiritual essence of Bhajane and Kunitha Bhajane. Initiated by the management, the club nurtures discipline, unity and cultural identity through devotional art.

It offers workshops, training sessions and performance opportunities to learn traditional rhythms, instruments and coordinated movements. Open to students from first to fourth year, the club welcomes all to experience devotion through music, movement and collective energy.

Grey Matter The Quiz and Debate Club of NMAMIT, established in 2009, is one of the oldest and most distinguished clubs on campus. Its primary objective is to cultivate a vibrant quizzing and debating culture by identifying and nurturing new talent. The club organises quizzes, debates, and Model United Nations (MUN) events on campus, while actively participating in external competitions. Its members have consistently brought recognition to the institution, securing numerous awards across these platforms.

Club Rachana is where creativity finds its true colours at NMAM Institute of Technology. More than just an art club, it’s a space where students come together to explore, learn, and share their love for art. From sketching and painting to digital doodling and crafts, the club helps members sharpen their skills through fun workshops and training sessions. Competitions and exhibitions give students the chance to showcase their talent and inspire others. At its heart, Club Rachana is about growing together, expressing freely, and making campus life more colourful.

Authorcraft, the literary club of NMAMIT, is a vibrant community that fosters creativity and self-expression. Through regular sessions that are both fun and interactive, members get to hone their writing skills and share their work. The club's open mic sessions provide a platform for individuals to express themselves. Members' works are showcased on the club's social media handle, giving them a wider audience. Authorcraft also publishes "Nirvana", an annual magazine of the club that features the best of the members' literary creations. The club represents NMAMIT at external events, showcasing its talent and creativity. With mega events that offer members a stage to express themselves, 'Steal the Spotlight', Authorcraft is the perfect haven for budding writers and performers to shine.

Yuj for Life, the Yoga Club of our college, is dedicated to promoting health, mindfulness, and inner balance. “Yuj” means union – reflecting the harmony of body, mind, and spirit. Through regular yoga sessions, workshops, and wellness activities, we encourage students to embrace yoga as a way of life, fostering fitness, self-awareness, and holistic living. Our club also actively showcases yoga performances during cultural events like Incredia and Aikya, spreading the message of wellness and balance to a wider audience.

Annadaana Club The Annadaana Club serves as a platform where compassion is translated into action. It reaches out to individuals and communities in need by providing food, clothing, educational materials, and other essential resources. Each initiative is guided by the belief that small acts of kindness can create meaningful change. The club’s mission extends beyond fulfilling basic needs, aiming to spread positivity and hope. By engaging students as volunteers, it fosters empathy, teamwork, and social responsibility. The Annadaana Club is committed to building a society where no one is left behind.

Aura is a student-driven club at NMAMIT committed to fostering compassion, kindness, and inclusivity. Its mission is to make a lasting difference in society through purposeful outreach programmes that uplift and support underserved groups. By involving students in donation drives, hair-donation initiatives, yoga sessions, and other service activities, Aura nurtures empathy and a strong sense of social responsibility. Through active participation and community engagement, the club cultivates a caring campus atmosphere where kindness and mutual respect thrive.

Clicz, the photography and videography club of NMAMIT, is a creative space for students passionate about capturing moments and expressing stories through visuals. The main objective of the club is to bring out the inner talent within students while honing their skills in photography, videography, and editing. Beyond capturing the spirit of campus life, Clicz plays a vital role in documenting cultural festivals and major college events, turning fleeting moments into lasting memories. Members of Clicz also participate enthusiastically in intercollegiate competitions and photography contests, showcasing their creativity and technical skills.

HackerEarth Hub NMAMIT is a student-led coding club, dedicated to fostering a competitive programming and web development culture through weekly contests and daily practice problem submissions focused on DSA and aptitude skills. The club supports consistent skill growth for its members, preparing them for coding competitions and placements with collaborative activities and hands-on web development opportunities. HackerEarth Hub NMAMIT provides a vibrant environment for aspiring programmers to grow through structured contests, daily practice, and collaborative web development experiences.

Kalanjali – The Dance Club is the vibrant hub for all dance enthusiasts at NMAMIT, dedicated to nurturing students’ passion for styles like classical, contemporary, hip-hop, and fusion through specialised crews under Kalanjali – Mudra (classical and expressive), Tiptoe (contemporary), and Ripple Factor Crew (RFC) (hip-hop and freestyle). Through regular practices and workshops, Kalanjali helps members sharpen their skills and perform confidently. The club’s flagship events include electrifying flash mobs, high-energy dance battles, and spectacular stage performances during major college celebrations like Incredia, Onam, Karnataka Rajyotsava, Ganesh Chaturthi, and other cultural fests. These events showcase Kalanjali members’ talent and dedication, inspiring a vibrant dance culture across campus.

Stereo Club is the official music club of NMAMIT, bringing together passionate singers, instrumentalists, rappers, music composers and music producers who share a love for music. The club actively performs on various cultural and festive occasions such as Janmastami, Ganesh Chaturthi, Onam, and Rajyotsava, adding vibrance to every celebration. Apart from stage performances, members regularly present prayer songs at the beginning of major events hosted in the college, creating a soulful start to the proceedings. The club also showcases its creativity beyond campus by releasing song covers on Stereo Club’s official YouTube and Instagram pages, reaching a wider audience and celebrating music digitally. On the competitive front, Stereo Club proudly represents the college in inter-collegiate fests, taking part in Battle of Bands and other music-based competitions, consistently displaying the talent and energy of its members. With a blend of tradition and modernity, Stereo Club not only entertains but also unites people through the universal language of music.

Taaleem is NMAMIT’s home for theatre and performance, where imagination takes the stage and expression knows no bounds. From witty mad ads, skits, mimes, and street plays to grand productions and short films, the club inspires students to explore diverse forms of storytelling while building teamwork and creative confidence. With a vibrant presence at college festivals such as Kannada Rajyotsava, Ganesh Chaturthi, Onam, Incredia, and intercollegiate fests, Taaleem brings theatre to life through captivating mythological productions, powerful social narratives, and performances that entertain, inspire, and leave a lasting impression

The Soft Skills and Communication Association (SACA) is NMAMIT’s flagship club and the nexus for campus communicators, serving as both a stage for seasoned orators and a sanctuary for those building their confidence. SACA members are central to campus life—orchestrating the Freshers' Orientation, emceeing major functions, and creating their own calendar of engaging events. The club’s most vital contribution is spearheading the institute-wide Employment Readiness Program (ERP), an annual undertaking that provides every third-year student with crucial training in professional conduct and behavioural interviews. Guided by the motto Connect, Communicate, Conquer, SACA is where communication is crafted into true leadership.

The COPE Mental Health Awareness Club The institution is committed to promoting student well-being by raising awareness, challenging stigmas, and providing a safe, supportive environment for open dialogue. Through peer support, educational initiatives, and outreach programmes, the COPE club equips students with tools to build resilience and foster a culture of mental health awareness. The club also organises interactive workshops, campaigns, and events that encourage students to share experiences, acquire knowledge, and grow together. Participation in COPE enables students to receive support for their own well-being while becoming advocates for positive change, contributing to a compassionate and health-conscious campus community.

Members of Clicz also participate enthusiastically in intercollegiate competitions and photography contests, showcasing their creativity and technical skills.

HackerEarth Hub HackerEarth Hub NMAMIT is a student-led coding club, dedicated to fostering a competitive programming and web development culture through weekly contests and daily practice problem submissions focused on DSA and aptitude skills. Kalanjali Kalanjali – The Dance Club is the vibrant hub for all dance enthusiasts at NMAMIT, dedicated to nurturing students’ passion for styles like classical, contemporary, hip-hop, and fusion through specialised crews under Kalanjali – Mudra (classical and expressive), Tiptoe (contemporary), and Ripple Factor Crew (RFC) (hip-hop and freestyle). Through regular practices and workshops, Kalanjali helps members sharpen their skills and perform confidently. These events showcase Kalanjali members’ talent and dedication, inspiring a vibrant dance culture across campus.

Stereo club Stereo Club is the official music club of NMAMIT, bringing together passionate singers, instrumentalists, rappers, music composers and music producers who share a love for music. Apart from stage performances, members regularly present prayer songs at the beginning of major events hosted in the college, creating a soulful start to the proceedings. The club also showcases its creativity beyond campus by releasing song covers on Stereo Club’s official YouTube and Instagram pages, reaching a wider audience and celebrating music digitally. With a blend of tradition and modernity, Stereo Club not only entertains but also unites people through the universal language of music.

At its heart, Club Rachana is about growing together, expressing freely, and making campus life more colourful.

headings.text: Talk on Breast Cancer Awareness by Dr. Smitha Rao, Breast Cancer & Endocrine Surgeon

paragraphs: NMAM Institute of Technology, Nitte, in association with the National Service Scheme (NSS) Unit and Rotary Club Nitte, organized a talk on Breast Cancer Awareness along with a Primary Breast Cancer Screening session at NMAMIT campus on 21st August 2026.
Ms. Tulsi Hariprasad, NSS volunteer delivered the welcome address and briefed about the session. This was followed by a video presentation on breast cancer awareness.

Resource person Dr. Smitha S. Rao, Breast & Endocrine Surgeon, K S Hegde Medical Academy, advised the students & attendees to take the HPV vaccination as a preventive measure, mentioning that it is not a drug that treats cancer, but one that helps prevent it. She also quoted the saying that genetics loads the gun, but environment & lifestyle pull the trigger. Dr. Rao emphasized that a girl should be taught from childhood what is normal for her body, so that any abnormality can be recognized early. She spoke about the importance of regular self-breast examination and periodic health check-ups in early detection of the disease. She also encouraged the engineering students present to work towards building devices that could help doctors assess breast health quickly and effectively.
Following the stage program, the Primary Breast Cancer Screening session was conducted for the attendees under the guidance of the medical team.

paragraphs: Nitte (Deemed to be University) offers Dual Degree Program in collaboration with the University of Wollongong (UOW), Australia for students of BTech in Computer Science Engineering at Nitte Mahalinga Adyanthaya Memorial Institute of Technology, Nitte with the approval of AICTE.

University of Wollongong, Australia is an Australian public research university located in the coastal city of Wollongong, New South Wales approximately 80 kilometres south of Sydney. It offers a variety of undergraduate, graduate and doctoral programs and is ranked 162 nd in QS World University Rankings 2024.

The Dual Degree Program is structured on a 2+2 model with students completing the 1st & 2nd year requirements at Nitte DU and the 3rd & 4th year requirements at University of Wollongong, Australia. The credits earned at Nitte DU are recognized by UOW, Australia and credits earned at UOW are recognized by Nitte DU. On successful completion of requirements, students earn a degree from the University of Wollongong as well as from Nitte DU simultaneously.

Pass in Class 12 or equivalent examination with not less than 60% marks as an aggregate in the optional subjects of Physics, Mathematics and Chemistry/ Biotechnology/ Biology/ Computer Science/ Electronics/ Information Technology, with English as one of the languages of study.
The candidate should have completed 17 years of age as on 31st December of the year of admission.
BTech Program in Computer Science Engineering

Nitte University in collaboration with Penn State University, Harrisburg (USA) is offering the options of Twinning / Dual Degree program in BTech (Computer Science Engineering) at Nitte Mahalinga Adyanthaya Memorial Institute of Technology, with the approval of AICTE.

Penn State University at Harrisburg (PSU) is one of the constituent campuses of the Pennsylvania State University. PSU is a public state-related land-grant research university with campuses and facilities throughout the State of Pennsylvania, USA offering a variety of undergraduate, graduate and doctoral programs. It is ranked 83 rd in the QS World University Rankings of 2024.

The Dual Degree Program is structured on a 2+2 model with students completing the 1st & 2nd year requirements at Nitte DU and the 3rd & 4th year requirements at Penn State University, Harrisburg. The credits earned at NitteDU are recognized by PSU, Harrisburg and credits earned at PSU are recognized by NitteDU. On successful completion of requirements, students earn a degree from the Penn State University as well as from NitteDU simultaneously.

The Twinning program is structured on a 2+1+1 model with students completing the 3rd year requirements at Penn State University, Harrisburg. The credits earned at PSU, Harrisburg are recognized towards the degree requirements, through a bipartite agreement between Nitte DU and PSU. Students who complete the program successfully, will receive B.Tech in Computer Science Engineering from Nitte (Deemed to be University).

Both the Dual and Twinning programs enable students to experience an international learning environment, train in advanced laboratories and enhance their cultural competence. The program also offers opportunities for networking that can be valuable for future career growth.

Pass in Class 12 or equivalent examination with not less than 60% marks as an aggregate in the optional subjects of Physics, Mathematics and Chemistry/ Biotechnology/ Biology/ Computer Science/ Electronics/ Information Technology, with English as one of the languages of study.
The candidate should have completed 17 years of age as on 31st December of the year of admission.

Nitte DU students participating in the Dual / twinning program will be subject to the standard academic regulations and performance standards of Penn State and will take the regular examinations. To be accepted into the semesters of study at PSU, students must have earned a minimum of 80 credits by the end of the second year at Nitte with a cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of 6.25 (Nitte DU Grading Scale) equivalent to 2.5 (Penn State grading scale).
Interested candidates may submit the application at apply.nitte.edu.in
Selection will be based on the basis of academic merit.

title: Research Policies & Framework - NMAMIT

headings.text: Objectives of NMAMIT & NMIT IP Policy
Evaluation of IP and Patent Filing Process

paragraphs: Intellectual Property (IP) refers to creation of the mind of any person (inventor) such as inventions, innovations, literary work, artistic works, designs, symbols, names, logos, and images. IP plays pivotal role in providing a competitive edge to organizations. Tangible assets like inventions, designs, software, brand name and other creative and innovative ideas are more valuable than physical assets. It is necessary to protect these creations in order to enable organizations to earn recognition or financial benefits. In this scenario, governments of various countries enable protection of innovative ideas through Intellectual Property Rights (IPR). Recently, IPR has become a central issue in the development of higher academic institutions. Faculty, research scholars, scientists, students and other personnel of NMAMIT and NMIT are actively engaged in various research and development activities of diversified nature. Many of these research and development leads to different forms of IP, which are likely to be commercially utilized unless protected by IPR. In this scenario, NMAMITand NMITencourage, facilitate, promote and safeguard scientific investigations and research of NMAMIT and NMIT Personnel. Common IP Policy aims to lay down the process for promotion and support to innovators of NMAMIT and NMIT for converting their innovative works into IP. A common IP policy also aims to set forth guidelines for ownership of IP developed at NMAMIT and NMIT by faculty who are directly or indirectly associated with the institutions, either in-house or outsource, sponsored unless specially covered by a policy to the contrary. The common IPR Cell will address specific cases by using this IP policy document as guidelines. The IP policy is expected to fulfill the commitment of both the Institutions in order to promote academic freedom and provide a beneficial environment for research and development.

Intellectual Property Rights denote specific legal rights of the inventors to hold and exercise Patents, Trademarks, Copyrights, Industrial Designs, etc. IPR aims to exclude third parties from exploiting the protected subject matter for a certain period of time (normally 20 years), without explicit authorization from the right holders. IPR owners can use or disclose their creations without fear of loss of control over their usage during the course of dissemination of their creation/invention. IP confers of exclusive rights in relation to the particular form in which ideas/information are expressed/manifested in the following manner:
Objectives of common IP policy:

NMAMIT and NMIT shall be the owners, with the creators specially stated as inventors for all the intellectual property inventions, software designs and specimens created by the creators who include faculty members, research scholars, students and those who make use of the resources of NMAMIT and NMIT.

The Inventions created by NMAMIT/NMIT personnel, shall be owned by the Institutions and inventors; the revenue generated out of such creations shall be shared in the ratio of 60:40 between the creator and NMAMIT/NMIT respectively. If inventors are from both the Institutions, the 40% share of the institution shall be shared between institutions. If an IP has emerged as a result of an Institutional/Industrial consultancy, sponsored to NMAMIT/NMIT the concerned industry and NMAMIT/NMIT shall own the IP. This however will not apply to those IP that are covered under specific MoUs where the action shall be carried out as per the provisions of the MoUs. If the IP is a result of funds sponsored by an outside agency, the IP will be shared between NMAMIT/NMIT and the sponsoring agency on case by case basis, as per MoU/Agreement/Undertaking between NMAMIT/NMIT and the outside agency.

A computer software may be patented, copyrighted, trademarked depending upon the IP content. A copyright software may be distributed for research and teaching purposes by its creator after obtaining appropriate undertaking to the effect that it will not be used for commercial purpose nor will it be transferred to any other party without explicit permission of NMAMIT / NMIT.

The common IPR cell will coordinate the activities associated with patenting with the help of external patent attorney. Initial evaluation of patentability of the IP will be carried out by the external agency for free. However, if IP is found to be acceptable for patent/trademark/copyright then NMAMIT/ NMIT will bear the entire patenting expenses; however, the patent will have to be filed with NMAMIT and NMIT as applicants and expenses will be shared by both the Institutes.

For patentable IP, an arrangement will be made for patent protection by filing patent protection (non-disclosure agreement) with the attorney. Confidentiality shall be maintained till the dates stipulated in the contract between the concerned parties. Once the IPR is published in the Journal of Indian Patent Office the inventor/creator is encouraged to publish the work in the interest of general public.

The inventions, wherein NMAMIT and NMIT are co-applicants shall be renewed annually at the consent of both the Institutions. The maintenance of patents granted in association with external agencies will be as per MOU established; however, if MOU established states that the patent ownership is with external agency and inventor, NMAMIT/NMIT will play no part in the maintenance of the patent.
NMAMIT/ NMIT shall be the owner of all copyright works including software and all connected teaching materials designed and developed by employees of NMAMIT/ NMIT.

Further, NMAMIT/ NMIT shall also be the owner of copyrights of works produced, including software and all teaching materials developed by persons not directly associated with NMAMIT/ NMIT, provided NMAMIT/ NMIT has made its contribution in the form of any of the resources. The ownership of copyright by NMAMIT/ NMIT will in no way deprive the claims of the creator/author to publish his/her contribution in a scholarly and intellectual way and they have the authority to improve, publish and propagate their works.
Copyright will also be governed by other rules and regulations framed for patents by various authorities concerned.
